Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Dysuria with foul-smelling urine and blood in urine.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started 6 days ago; persistent with fluctuating lower abdominal pain.
- Associated symptoms: Lower abdominal pain (midline) rated about 7/10; no fever; no back/loin pain; able to eat and drink.
- Urinary: Able to pass urine; blood in urine noted (spotting) for 6 days.
- Past medical history: IBS; no other medical problems or surgeries reported.
- Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg, three times daily; route not documented.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.
- Social history: Lives with friends; works as a support worker; drinks alcohol occasionally (about one glass of wine per week); non-smoker.
- Menstrual/reproductive: Regular periods; no vaginal discharge; not described as pregnant.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- No vitals or laboratory/imaging results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis)
   - Assessment: Clinical presentation suggests UTI (dysuria, foul-smelling urine, hematuria, suprapubic/midline lower abdominal pain; no fever).
   - Differential diagnoses: Urethritis; pyelonephritis less likely given absence of fever and loin/back pain.
   - Investigations: Urinalysis or urine culture not performed/not planned at this time.
   - Treatment: Empiric antibiotic therapy for 3 days; specific antibiotic name not documented in transcript.
   - Additional management: Advise high fluid intake (2.5–3 liters/day); cranberry juice recommended; urine-acidity–modifying sachets available at pharmacy (details to be recorded).
   - Follow-up/referral: If symptoms worsen or fever develops, or if not resolving with treatment, contact clinician for re-evaluation. If infections become recurrent, discuss further management.

- Pharmacy logistics
  - Antibiotics to be sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy; pickup expected in about an hour to lunchtime.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs; objective physical exam findings; urinalysis results; pregnancy/test-of-eligibility status; full medications reconciliation; specific antibiotic name and route.
